summary: This educational web app helps people learn how locations on Earth can serve as analogs for future Moon bases and Mars missions. Users explore planetary environments, compare Earth locations with Mars using an interactive map, and take challenges that test their knowledge of terrain, climate, geology, and rover operations. The project also features a 3D rover simulation on a NASA Mars map, where players can experience simulated missions. By combining learning, challenges, and gameplay, the project makes planetary science more engaging and shows how Earth-based research can help prepare for future space exploration.
details:
Operation Red Rock is an educational web app that teaches users how Earth locations can serve as analogs for future permanent Moon bases and Mars missions. Users explore planetary sites on an interactive map, learn how terrain, geology, and climate affect mission planning, and take challenges to test their understanding. The project also features a 3D rover simulator on a NASA Mars map, combining learning with play.

The app was built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, Three.js, and WebGL, and runs in a standard web browser without special hardware. We designed it to make planetary science engaging through research, visual exploration, challenges, and simulation. Super Intelligence tools supported development and media creation: Antigravity and Copilot for programming, ElevenLabs for audio, and Gemini for video. The team reviews generated media and checks scientific information against cited sources.
